Inline R in markdown

Source: R/prose-block.R
inline_r.Rd

Writes the value of every `r expr` in a markdown string into the text, as knitr does for inline code: each expression is evaluated with the objects in data in scope, and its value replaces the code.

Usage

inline_r(text, data = list())

Arguments

text

A markdown string.

data

A named list of objects the expressions can use.

Value

The markdown string with the values written in.

Details

Left alone: code in fenced blocks, other inline code, and inline code written between double backticks to show the syntax (`` `r x` ``). Code in a block indented by four spaces is evaluated, as knitr does.

A value has to be a vector of at most 100 elements. A number is written in full (1000000, not 1e+06) and several values are joined by commas. NULL writes nothing. When the code holds several expressions, the value of the last one is written.

Each expression is evaluated in a fresh environment whose parent is the global environment. data is always bound there (NULL when the list has none), so it never resolves to utils::data. <<- writes to the global environment, which all sessions of a Shiny app share.

Examples

inline_r("There are `r nrow(data)` cars.", list(data = mtcars))
#> [1] "There are 32 cars."
